picks.file: Haec est nobilis florens illa Neapolis, Campaniae civitas.jpg
picks.what: Bird’s-eye view, colored engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 1
picks.why: highest-resolution colored copy; harbor, Castel Nuovo and the street grid drawn in detail; legend strip trimmed

picks.file: Gezicht op de haven met een vuurtoren en een paleis te Napels Le Mole, le Cinosura, et le Castell Novo, à Naples (titel op object) Paleizen en monumenten in Venetië, Livorno, Napels en Rome (serietitel), BI-1962-1072-61.jpg
picks.what: The harbor mole, lighthouse and Castel Nuovo, etching (Rijksmuseum)
picks.who: unknown artist, after Johann Wilhelm Baur and Melchior Küsel
picks.why: only usable P2 view; titled harbor scene with the lighthouse and Castel Nuovo; trimmed to the plate

picks.file: Veduta di Napoli dalla Villa Ruffo a Capodimonte.jpg
picks.what: View from Villa Ruffo at Capodimonte, engraving
picks.why: general view over the rooftops to Castel Sant’Elmo and the bay; caption trimmed

picks.file: N°14. Veduta di Napoli - btv1b53264245n (1 of 2).jpg
picks.what: The city and the bay with Vesuvius, photograph (Bibliothèque nationale de France)
picks.why: classic view with Vesuvius over the bay and city; firm date; mount trimmed

picks.what: The harbor and Castel Sant’Elmo, photograph
picks.why: general view across the harbor to the hill with Castel Sant’Elmo; low resolution (1024 px)

gaps: P0: none; P6: no modern photograph among the candidates (#35–#40 are photochroms and a Bruegel painting misdated by their uploaders)
notes: #28 (color photochrom of the harbor with Castel Sant’Elmo, 1890s) is a good alternative to Rive’s 1865 photograph if color is preferred; the two are too close in date to use both. #39 (Bruegel, Bay of Naples, about 1563) is a fine color alternative for P1 but shows a naval scene. #15 (Drayton engraving) carries a doubtful date of 1800 and was skipped. #12/#13 (optical views) are only dated 1700–1799.
